items.prompt: Which organelle is the main site of ATP production in eukaryotic cells?

options.label: Golgi apparatus
Lysosome
Ribosome
Mitochondrion

rubric: Mitochondria carry out most cellular respiration and make ATP.
Golgi is often confused because it is involved in processing, not energy.

items.prompt: What is the main molecular component of the cell membrane's basic structure?

options.label: Protein sheet layer
Cellulose fibre wall
Nucleic acid chain
Phospholipid bilayer

rubric: Membranes are built on a phospholipid bilayer.
Cellulose belongs to plant cell walls, not membranes.

items.prompt: Which structure contains the DNA of a eukaryotic cell?

options.label: Vacuole
Cytoskeleton
Nucleus
Peroxisome

rubric: Eukaryotic DNA is enclosed in the nucleus.
Other organelles are not the main DNA store.

items.prompt: What is the term for the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane?

options.label: Endocytosis
Active transport
Osmosis
Exocytosis

rubric: Osmosis is water diffusion across a membrane.
Endo- and exocytosis move bulk material in vesicles.

items.prompt: In which phase of the cell cycle is DNA replicated?

options.label: Cytokinesis
S phase
G2 phase
Prophase

rubric: S stands for synthesis of DNA.
Prophase is often wrongly chosen because chromosomes become visible then.

items.prompt: Which of the following are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells? Select all that apply.

options.label: Nucleus
Ribosomes
Mitochondria
DNA
Plasma membrane

rubric: All cells have ribosomes, a plasma membrane and DNA.
Nucleus and mitochondria are eukaryote-only.

items.prompt: A student is labelling a diagram of a plant cell for a quiz. She must mark the structure outside the plasma membrane that gives the cell a rigid shape. Which structure should she label?

options.label: Centrosome
Cell wall
Nuclear envelope
Smooth ER

rubric: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall outside the membrane.
The nuclear envelope is a membrane inside the cell.

items.prompt: Why can small nonpolar molecules such as oxygen cross the membrane without a transport protein?

options.label: They bind to receptors that carry them across
They are pushed through by ATP-driven pumps
They are small enough to pass through open pores in the membrane
They dissolve in the hydrophobic lipid interior of the bilayer

rubric: Nonpolar molecules dissolve in the lipid core.
Pumps and pores are wrong because simple diffusion needs neither.

items.prompt: How does the rough ER differ in function from the smooth ER?

options.label: Rough ER stores DNA; smooth ER stores calcium only
Rough ER makes lipids for membranes; smooth ER makes proteins
Rough ER makes proteins; smooth ER makes lipids
Rough ER digests waste; smooth ER packages secretions

rubric: Ribosomes on rough ER make proteins; smooth ER makes lipids.
Swapping roles is a common confusion.

items.prompt: A red blood cell is placed in pure water. What is the most likely outcome and why?

options.label: It stays the same because the membrane blocks all water
It shrinks because salts rush out of the cell
It shrinks because water leaves toward the lower solute side
It swells and may burst because water enters by osmosis

rubric: Water moves toward higher solute concentration inside the cell.
Shrinking is the outcome in a hypertonic solution, not pure water.

items.prompt: Which statement best explains the difference between facilitated diffusion and active transport?

options.label: Facilitated diffusion uses ATP to move substances against a gradient
Active transport uses energy to move substances against their gradient
Facilitated diffusion moves substances through the lipid bilayer without any protein help
Active transport needs no protein while facilitated diffusion does

rubric: Active transport moves solutes uphill using energy.
Facilitated diffusion is passive and follows the gradient.

items.prompt: Why is mitosis important for a multicellular organism such as a human?

options.label: It produces gametes with half the chromosomes
It creates new genetic combinations in body cells
It turns unspecialised body cells into different specialised cell types
It makes identical cells for growth and repair

rubric: Mitosis yields identical diploid daughter cells.
Halving chromosomes describes meiosis.

items.prompt: Which statements correctly explain why a eukaryotic cell is considered more compartmentalised than a prokaryotic cell? Select all that apply.

options.label: The nucleus separates DNA from the cytoplasm
Prokaryotes lack a cell membrane, so no reactions are separated
Lysosomes keep digestive enzymes away from the rest of the cell
Membrane-bound organelles separate different reactions

rubric: Organelles, nucleus and lysosomes create separate compartments.
Prokaryotes do have ribosomes.

items.prompt: A lab technician sees that a cell type that secretes large amounts of digestive enzymes has an extensive rough ER and many Golgi stacks. She wants to explain this to a new student. Which explanation is best?

options.label: Both organelles make the ATP that powers enzyme secretion from the cell
The rough ER and Golgi keep extra copies of the DNA for the enzyme genes
The Golgi makes the enzyme proteins and the rough ER breaks down the excess
Rough ER makes secreted proteins; the Golgi modifies and packages them

rubric: Proteins for secretion are synthesised on rough ER then processed in Golgi.
Reversing the roles confuses synthesis and packaging.

items.prompt: A pancreatic cell secretes large amounts of digestive enzymes. Which organelle would you expect to be especially abundant in it?

options.label: Peroxisomes
Rough ER
Chloroplasts
Smooth ER

rubric: Secreted proteins are made on ribosomes bound to rough ER, so secretory cells have a lot of it.
Smooth ER is the tempting distractor, but it makes lipids and detoxifies rather than making proteins.

items.prompt: Why do phospholipids in water assemble into a bilayer with the fatty acid tails facing inward?

options.label: Hydrophilic tails bond covalently, so they join in the center
Charged heads repel each other, so tails get pushed inward
Tails are attracted to proteins, so they gather in the core
Hydrophobic tails avoid water, so they cluster away from it

rubric: Nonpolar tails are hydrophobic and are shielded from water in the interior of the bilayer.
Distractors invoke covalent bonding, head repulsion or protein attraction, none of which drives bilayer formation.

items.prompt: What is the main role of the Golgi apparatus in a eukaryotic cell?

options.label: Builds proteins by linking free amino acids on mRNA
Makes most of the cell's ATP from glucose using oxygen
Stores the cell's DNA as chromatin inside a envelope
Modifies, sorts and packages proteins into vesicles

rubric: The Golgi finishes, sorts and ships proteins and lipids.
Protein synthesis (ribosomes) and ATP production (mitochondria) are common mix-ups.

items.prompt: A red blood cell is placed in pure water. What is most likely to happen, and why?

options.label: It stays unchanged, because the membrane blocks all water movement
It swells and may burst, because solutes rush in by active transport
It shrinks and may shrivel, because water moves out toward the solutes
It swells and may burst, because water moves in by osmosis

rubric: Pure water is hypotonic to the cytoplasm, so water enters by osmosis.
Shrinking describes a hypertonic solution; the other options misstate membrane permeability or transport.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly describes the role of mitochondria in eukaryotic cells?

options.label: They digest worn-out organelles with hydrolytic enzymes
They use oxygen to make most of the cell's ATP
They assemble ribosomal subunits in the nucleolus region
They convert light energy into chemical energy in sugars

rubric: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and make most ATP.
Light conversion is chloroplasts and digestion is lysosomes.

items.prompt: Which statements correctly describe facilitated diffusion across a membrane? Select all that apply.

options.label: It requires direct hydrolysis of ATP
It needs no direct cellular energy input
Substances move against their concentration gradient
It uses channel or carrier proteins
Substances move down their concentration gradient

rubric: Facilitated diffusion is passive: proteins help, but movement follows the gradient with no ATP.
Direct ATP use and movement against a gradient describe active transport.

items.prompt: A microscopist examines a single-celled organism. It has no nucleus, its circular DNA lies free in the cytoplasm, it has 70S ribosomes, and it is surrounded by a cell wall. How should the organism be classified, and why?

options.label: Eukaryote, because circular DNA is typical of plant cells
Prokaryote, because cell walls occur only in prokaryotes and never in eukaryotes
Eukaryote, because it has ribosomes and a cell wall
Prokaryote, because its DNA is not inside a nuclear envelope

rubric: The defining feature is DNA not enclosed by a nuclear envelope, with a nucleoid region instead.
Ribosomes and cell walls occur in both groups, so they do not separate prokaryotes from eukaryotes.

items.prompt: A cube-shaped cell has sides of 4 micrometres. What is its surface area to volume ratio (in units of 1/micrometre)?
rubric: Surface area is 6 x 16 = 96 and volume is 64, so the ratio is 1.5.
Distractors come from using the wrong formula, such as 6 alone or the ratio for a 1-micrometre side.

items.prompt: Each cycle of the Na+/K+ pump uses 1 ATP to move 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ into the cell. How many Na+ are moved out when the cell uses 4 ATP?
rubric: 4 ATP means 4 cycles, and 4 x 3 = 12 Na+ moved out.
8 is the K+ moved in, and 20 comes from adding both ions per cycle.

items.prompt: A human somatic cell has 46 chromosomes in G1. How many chromatids does it contain at prophase of mitosis?
rubric: DNA replicates in S phase, so each of the 46 chromosomes has 2 sister chromatids, giving 92.
46 ignores replication, and 184 double-counts it.

items.prompt: Cyanide blocks the last electron carrier in the electron transport chain of mitochondria. What is the immediate effect on a cell?

options.label: Glycolysis stops at once because it needs the electron chain
ATP production by oxidative phosphorylation drops sharply
Protein folding in the rough ER stops as the only effect
Oxygen use rises as the cell compensates for the block

rubric: Blocking electron flow collapses the proton gradient and so ATP synthase output.
Glycolysis does not need the electron transport chain, so it can continue briefly.

items.prompt: Which route would a newly made protein destined for secretion from the cell follow?

options.label: Rough ER, Golgi, secretory vesicle, then plasma membrane
Free ribosome, mitochondrion, vesicle, then exterior
Nucleus, lysosome, Golgi, then plasma membrane
Golgi, rough ER, vesicle, then plasma membrane

rubric: Secreted proteins enter the rough ER, move to the Golgi, then leave in vesicles that fuse with the plasma membrane.
The other routes put organelles in the wrong order or use organelles not in the secretory pathway.

items.prompt: Red blood cells are isotonic in 0.9% NaCl. In which of these solutions would they shrink? Select all that apply.

options.label: 3% NaCl
1.8% NaCl
Distilled water
0.9% NaCl
0.1% NaCl

rubric: Solutions more concentrated than 0.9% are hypertonic, so water leaves the cells and they shrink.
0.9% causes no net change, while 0.1% and distilled water are hypotonic and cause swelling.

items.prompt: A lab adds colchicine, which prevents spindle microtubules from forming, to a dividing cell culture. Several hours later, microscopy shows many cells with condensed chromosomes. At which stage have most arrested cells stopped?

options.label: S phase, with DNA replication halted partway through
Cytokinesis, with a cleavage furrow but two separate nuclei
G1, with uncondensed chromatin waiting for a growth signal
Mitosis, with chromosomes that cannot be aligned or pulled apart

rubric: Without a spindle, chromosomes cannot align and separate, so cells stall in mitosis (prometaphase or metaphase) with condensed chromosomes.
The other stages do not involve condensed chromosomes or depend on the spindle in the same way.

items.prompt: A red blood cell with an internal solute concentration of about 300 mOsm is placed in a solution of an impermeant solute at 150 mOsm. What happens to the cell?

options.label: Water enters and the cell swells, possibly lysing
Nothing changes because the membrane is selectively permeable
Water leaves and the cell shrinks, becoming crenated
Solute enters until both concentrations are equal

rubric: The solution is hypotonic, so water moves into the cell by osmosis and the cell swells.
Distractors reverse the direction of water movement or ignore that osmosis occurs across selective membranes.

items.prompt: The Na+/K+ ATPase moves 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in per ATP hydrolysed. After a cell hydrolyses 30 ATP through this pump, what is the net number of positive charges moved out?
rubric: Each cycle moves 3 positive charges out and 2 in, so net 1 per ATP; 30 ATP gives 30.
Distractors report only Na+ out (90), only K+ in (60) or the gross total (150).

items.prompt: A human somatic cell has 46 chromosomes in G1. How many DNA molecules (chromatids) does it contain in G2, just before mitosis begins?
rubric: S phase replicates each chromosome into two sister chromatids, giving 92 DNA molecules.
Distractors confuse haploid number, G1 count or double-count the replication.

items.prompt: A cuboidal cell has sides of 2 µm. It grows until its sides are 4 µm. Using surface area / volume = 6/side, how does the ratio change?

options.label: It doubles from 1.5 to 3
It quarters from 3 to 0.75
It halves from 3 to 1.5
It stays the same at 3

rubric: SA/V = 6/side gives 3 for 2 µm and 1.5 for 4 µm, so it halves.
Distractors treat the ratio as unchanged, inverted or scaling with the square of the size.

items.prompt: A pancreatic cell makes a secreted enzyme. Which sequence correctly traces the enzyme from synthesis to release?

options.label: Rough ER, Golgi apparatus, secretory vesicle, plasma membrane
Smooth ER, mitochondrion, Golgi, vesicle, plasma membrane
Rough ER, lysosome, secretory vesicle, Golgi, plasma membrane
Free ribosome, nucleus, Golgi, lysosome, plasma membrane

rubric: Secreted proteins are made on the rough ER, modified in the Golgi, packaged in vesicles and exocytosed.
Distractors insert the nucleus, mitochondria or lysosomes into the secretory route or reverse the Golgi and vesicle.

items.prompt: Glucose enters a cell through a GLUT carrier down its concentration gradient. Which statements correctly describe this process? Select all that apply.

options.label: Carriers move glucose against its gradient
It stops being net inward when concentrations are equal
Net movement continues after concentrations equalise
It needs no direct ATP hydrolysis
The rate saturates when all carriers are occupied

rubric: Facilitated diffusion is passive, saturable and ends in net terms at equilibrium.
Distractors describe active transport features: movement continuing at equilibrium or uphill.

items.prompt: In an onion root tip, a student counts 200 cells: 120 in interphase and 80 in mitotic stages. The full cell cycle for these cells lasts 20 hours. Assuming the proportion of cells reflects time spent, about how long does interphase last?

options.label: 12 hours
16 hours
8 hours
14 hours

rubric: Distractors use the mitotic fraction (8 h) or miscalculate proportions.

items.prompt: Cells that import glucose through SGLT (a Na+-coupled symporter) are treated with ouabain, which blocks the Na+/K+ ATPase. Glucose uptake falls over several minutes. Which explanation fits best?

options.label: SGLT needs ATP hydrolysed directly by the transporter itself
Glucose is no longer phosphorylated, so it leaves the cell
The Na+ gradient dissipates, removing the energy that drives SGLT
Ouabain blocks the glucose binding site on SGLT directly

rubric: Secondary active transport depends on the Na+ gradient the pump maintains; blocking the pump collapses it gradually.
Distractors treat SGLT as primary active transport or invent a direct binding effect.

items.prompt: Cultured cells are treated with colchicine, which prevents microtubule polymerisation. Flow cytometry shows a large rise in cells with 4C DNA content, and microscopy shows cells without anaphase. What best explains this?

options.label: DNA replication is blocked, so cells stall in early S phase with partly replicated DNA
Without a spindle the checkpoint holds cells in mitosis before anaphase
Cells exit mitosis normally and re-enter G1 with doubled DNA after skipping anaphase
Cytokinesis fails after anaphase, so cells become binucleate with a 4C DNA content

rubric: No spindle means unattached kinetochores, so the spindle checkpoint arrests cells at metaphase with 4C DNA.
Distractors place the block in S phase, after anaphase or assume normal exit.

items.prompt: Fish moved from warm to cold water increase the proportion of unsaturated phospholipid tails in their membranes. Which analysis explains the benefit?

options.label: Unsaturated tails make the membrane fully impermeable to water
Unsaturated tails raise cholesterol content, which freezes the lipids
Kinked tails pack loosely, keeping the membrane fluid in cold
Kinked tails pack tightly, which strengthens the membrane against cold damage

rubric: Double bonds create kinks that reduce packing and preserve fluidity at low temperature.
Distractors reverse packing effects or invent unrelated consequences.

items.prompt: A drug inhibits phosphodiesterase in cells responding to a hormone through a G protein and cAMP. Compared with untreated cells, what is the most likely result after hormone exposure?

options.label: cAMP is broken down faster, so the response is shortened
Adenylyl cyclase is inactivated, so no cAMP is made
The G protein is locked inactive, so the receptor is silenced
cAMP persists longer, so downstream signalling is prolonged

rubric: Phosphodiesterase degrades cAMP; inhibiting it prolongs the signal.
Distractors reverse the enzyme's role or target the wrong step.

items.prompt: A cell expresses a mutant secretory protein whose N-terminal signal sequence is deleted. Pulse-labelling shows the protein is made at normal levels. Where would it most likely be found?

options.label: Inside the rough ER lumen, awaiting transport
In the extracellular fluid, secreted by default
Free in the cytosol, never entering the ER
Within Golgi vesicles, unmodified

rubric: The signal sequence directs ribosomes to the ER; without it the protein is made on free ribosomes and stays in the cytosol.
Distractors assume the protein still enters the secretory pathway.

items.prompt: Which observations about mitochondria best support the endosymbiotic origin of the organelle? Select all that apply.

options.label: Ribosomes similar in size to bacterial ribosomes
A nuclear envelope surrounding the organelle
Packaging of its DNA into linear chromosomes with introns
A circular genome lacking histones
Division by binary fission-like splitting

rubric: Bacterial-like genome, ribosomes and division support an endosymbiotic origin.
Distractors describe eukaryotic nuclear features that would not indicate bacterial ancestry.

items.prompt: Cells lacking functional p53 are exposed to a DNA-damaging agent. Unlike normal cells, they do not arrest, and they replicate damaged DNA. Flow cytometry shows many cells entering S phase with breaks. Which failure best explains this?

options.label: The G1/S checkpoint failed to halt the cycle in response to damage
The spindle checkpoint failed to detect unattached kinetochores
The cells cannot make cyclin proteins and so never leave G1
Cytokinesis failed after mitosis, giving polyploid cells

rubric: p53 normally halts cells at G1/S when DNA is damaged; its loss lets damaged cells enter S phase.
Distractors name other checkpoints or defects that do not match entry into S phase.

items.prompt: Cultured animal cells are treated with ouabain, which blocks the Na+/K+ ATPase. Within an hour the cells swell. Which chain of events best explains the swelling?

options.label: Na+ keeps leaking in with no pumping out, internal solute content rises, and water follows by osmosis
ATP accumulates unused in the cytosol, raising internal osmolarity until water is drawn in through the membrane
Loss of the pump halts membrane retrieval after exocytosis, so surface area expands and the cell enlarges
Blocked pumping lets K+ build up inside, the membrane depolarizes, and this opens aquaporins so water flows in

rubric: The pump maintains low internal Na+; without it, net solute gain drives osmotic water entry.
Distractors invoke depolarization opening aquaporins, ATP accumulation, or membrane retrieval, none of which causes swelling.

items.prompt: In a pulse-chase experiment, wild-type cells move a labeled secretory protein from rough ER to Golgi to secretory vesicles. In a mutant, the label stays in the rough ER and never reaches the Golgi, though the protein enters the ER and folds correctly. Which defect is most consistent?

options.label: Failure of the signal recognition particle to bind the signal sequence of the nascent chain
Failure to add mannose-6-phosphate to the protein in the Golgi lumen after it arrives
Failure to form clathrin-coated vesicles at the plasma membrane during endocytosis
Failure to bud COPII-coated transport vesicles from ER exit sites toward the Golgi

rubric: Protein enters and folds in the ER but cannot leave, which points to ER-to-Golgi vesicle budding (COPII).
Signal recognition and Golgi tagging are either already completed or occur downstream of the observed block.

items.prompt: Cells are exposed to UV that damages DNA. Normal cells arrest before S phase, but a mutant line enters S phase and replicates damaged DNA. The mutant makes normal cyclin E and CDK2 but no p21. Which missing step best explains this?

options.label: Loading of MCM helicases onto origins, which is required before any DNA replication can begin
Damage-triggered cyclin B degradation, which normally prevents the cell from entering mitosis
p53-driven induction of p21, which inhibits cyclin-CDK complexes and holds cells at G1/S
Spindle checkpoint signaling from unattached kinetochores, which normally delays the onset of anaphase

rubric: p21 is induced by p53 after damage and inhibits cyclin E-CDK2, enforcing the G1/S arrest.
The other options act at G2/M or metaphase-anaphase, or would block S phase rather than permit it.

items.prompt: Isolated mitochondria given substrate and ADP consume O2 at a steady rate. Adding the uncoupler DNP raises O2 consumption while ATP synthesis falls. Why does O2 consumption rise?

options.label: DNP stimulates citric acid cycle enzymes directly, which doubles the NADH supply reaching complex I
Dissipating the proton gradient removes back-pressure on the electron transport chain, so it runs faster
DNP donates electrons directly to oxygen, bypassing complex IV and adding extra respiration
Falling ATP activates ATP synthase in reverse, which pulls more electrons through the chain

rubric: Uncoupling collapses the proton motive force, which relieves inhibition of electron flow so O2 use rises with no ATP gain.
Distractors invent direct electron donation, reverse synthase action, or enzyme stimulation by DNP.

items.prompt: In a FRAP experiment, a GFP-tagged membrane protein recovers only 20% of fluorescence in a bleached spot over 10 minutes, while a fluorescent lipid in the same membrane recovers fully within seconds. Which interpretation is best supported?

options.label: Most of the protein is immobilized, e.g. by cytoskeletal anchoring, while lipids diffuse freely
The membrane is in a gel phase at that temperature, which slows the protein and the lipid similarly
The bleached GFP is degraded faster than new protein is made, so the spot cannot refill
The protein moves mainly by vesicle transport, so lateral diffusion in the bilayer contributes little

rubric: Free lipid diffusion with limited protein recovery indicates a large immobile protein fraction, such as tethering.
A gel phase would have immobilized the lipid too; degradation and vesicle-only movement are not implied by the data.

items.prompt: Cells lack the Golgi enzyme that adds mannose-6-phosphate to lysosomal hydrolases. Which outcomes would you expect? Select all that apply.

options.label: Hydrolases are misrouted into mitochondria through the TOM import complex
Hydrolase synthesis stops because ribosomes cannot translate the hydrolase mRNAs
Hydrolases are secreted into the extracellular medium instead of being delivered to lysosomes
Undigested material accumulates in vesicles because lysosomes lack enough active hydrolases
Hydrolases are still made on the rough ER and enter its lumen normally

rubric: Without the M6P tag, enzymes follow the default secretory route, leaving lysosomes deficient so substrates accumulate.
Translation and ER entry occur upstream of tagging and are unaffected; mitochondrial import uses different signals.

items.prompt: A lab measures uptake of solute X into red blood cells. Uptake rises linearly with external concentration up to the highest level tested, is unchanged by a protein-modifying reagent, and roughly doubles when X is chemically made more lipophilic. Which transport mode best fits, and why?

options.label: Channel-mediated diffusion, because open pores give linear uptake that would speed up with lipophilicity
Facilitated diffusion by a carrier, because it is passive and the rate increases with the concentration gradient
Primary active transport, because the rate rises as more pumps engage when substrate concentration increases
Simple diffusion, because uptake is non-saturable, insensitive to protein modification, and tracks lipid solubility

rubric: Linear, non-saturable uptake that ignores protein inactivation and scales with lipophilicity indicates passage through the bilayer.
Carriers saturate and are protein-sensitive; pumps and channels would also depend on proteins and not on solute lipophilicity.

items.prompt: You must decide whether protein P is in the mitochondrial matrix or the intermembrane space, using isolated intact mitochondria. Criteria: the method must distinguish the two compartments and keep the inner membrane intact. Which design is best?

options.label: Stain intact mitochondria with a membrane-impermeant dye and check whether P is labeled; labeling means P is in the matrix, no labeling means it is in the intermembrane space
Add detergent to dissolve all membranes, then add protease and compare digestion with an untreated sample
Treat intact mitochondria with protease alone, with no membrane disruption; P is digested if it is in the matrix and protected if it is in the intermembrane space
Rupture only the outer membrane by osmotic swelling, then add protease; P is digested if in the intermembrane space, protected if in the matrix

rubric: Selective outer-membrane rupture exposes the intermembrane space but not the matrix, so protease protection discriminates them.
Distractors reverse the logic, use a dye that cannot reach the matrix, or destroy compartments with detergent.

items.prompt: Serum-starved fibroblasts incorporate no BrdU over 24 h. A student concludes they have permanently left the cell cycle. Which critique is strongest?

options.label: BrdU is incorporated during G1, so a lack of label means the cells are probably stuck in G2 rather than out of the cycle
Starvation should have caused apoptosis, so the surviving cells must be cycling slowly rather than arrested, and a 24 h window cannot show this
No label shows only that S phase did not occur for 24 h; re-adding serum and testing BrdU uptake would assess reversibility
BrdU labels only mitotic cells, so the assay cannot report on DNA replication, and a mitotic index should be used in its place

rubric: Absence of S phase over a fixed window does not show permanence; quiescent cells can re-enter the cycle.
Distractors misstate what BrdU marks (S phase) or assume apoptosis or G2 arrest without evidence.

items.prompt: A GFP fusion of protein Q appears nuclear when overexpressed. A lab wants to claim endogenous Q is nuclear. Criteria: minimize artifacts from the tag and from expression level. Which approach is best?

options.label: Run a western blot of lysate to confirm the fusion has the expected size, which shows it is localized correctly
Increase expression further so the signal is brighter and any minor cellular pools become visible
Repeat the same construct in a second cell line, since agreement across lines proves native localization
Immunostain endogenous Q with an antibody and compare with a low-expression tagged version to check agreement

rubric: Detecting the untagged endogenous protein and comparing with low-level tagged protein directly addresses tag and overexpression artifacts.
Higher expression worsens mislocalization, another cell line keeps both artifacts, and a blot reports size, not location.

items.prompt: A lab needs cells synchronized at G1/S, reversibly, with most cells recovering and little mitotic disruption, to follow S phase in a time course. Which method is the best choice?

options.label: Nocodazole arrest, which holds cells in prometaphase and releases them into G1 rather than S
Double thymidine block, which reversibly stalls replication and releases cells together into S phase
Serum starvation for a week, which holds cells in G0 and gives tight release into S phase
Mitotic shake-off of rounded cells, which isolates mitotic cells and releases them straight into S

rubric: Excess thymidine reversibly stalls cells at G1/S, and release gives a synchronous S-phase wave.
Other methods start cells at mitosis or G0, giving a different entry point or looser synchrony.

items.prompt: A student claims bacteria must make ATP inefficiently because they lack mitochondria. Which critique is best?

options.label: Bacterial ribosomes are larger than eukaryotic ones, so protein synthesis costs much less ATP overall
Bacteria use electron transport and ATP synthase in the plasma membrane, driven by a proton gradient
Bacteria contain tiny mitochondria-like organelles that are too small to be seen by light microscopy
Bacteria rely on fermentation alone, which yields as much ATP per glucose as aerobic respiration does

rubric: Prokaryotes use their plasma membrane for chemiosmotic ATP synthesis, so lacking mitochondria does not imply poor efficiency.
Distractors state false facts: fermentation yields far less ATP, bacterial ribosomes are smaller, and bacteria have no such organelles.

items.prompt: After treatment with drug Z, cells become binucleate with 4N total DNA content and no further division. Which conclusions are justified by this data alone? Select all that apply.

options.label: Z inhibits spindle assembly
Chromosome segregation into two nuclei took place
Z blocks entry into S phase
The block lies at or after the final steps of mitosis, such as cytokinesis
DNA replication was completed before the block occurred

rubric: 4N content in two nuclei shows replication and segregation occurred, placing the failure at or after cytokinesis.
Blocked spindle assembly or S-phase entry would not yield two separated nuclei with replicated DNA.

items.prompt: A team designs an antibiotic for a bacterial infection. Criteria: selective toxicity to bacteria, activity against growing cells, and no toxicity to human mitochondria. Four targets are proposed. Which is the best choice?

options.label: The phospholipid bilayer of the plasma membrane, which is easy to reach and essential in growing cells
Peptidoglycan cross-linking in the cell wall, a structure absent from human cells and from mitochondria
Bacterial ATP synthase, which is essential for growth and similar in structure to the mitochondrial enzyme
Bacterial 70S ribosomes, which differ from human cytosolic 80S ribosomes and so spare human protein synthesis

rubric: Peptidoglycan synthesis is bacteria-specific, acts on growing cells, and has no mitochondrial counterpart.
Ribosome inhibitors can hit mitochondrial ribosomes, while membrane lipids and ATP synthase are shared with human cells.

items.prompt: A student claims intestinal glucose uptake through SGLT1 is independent of ATP because SGLT1 itself does not hydrolyze ATP. Which critique of this claim is best?

options.label: The claim is sound, because SGLT1 is a facilitated-diffusion carrier that moves glucose down its own gradient.
The claim fails, because SGLT1 is a primary pump that hydrolyzes ATP to move glucose against its gradient.
Uptake depends indirectly on ATP, because the Na+/K+ ATPase maintains the Na+ gradient that drives SGLT1 cotransport.
The claim is sound, because the Na+ gradient is a fixed membrane property that persists without any ATP input.

rubric: SGLT1 is secondary active transport powered by the Na+ gradient that the ATPase sustains.
Distractors treat it as passive or as a direct ATPase.

items.prompt: Cells treated with brefeldin A, which collapses the Golgi into the ER, still secrete protein Y at normal rates. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.label: Protein Y is probably released by cell lysis, since regulated secretion routes usually depend on an intact Golgi apparatus.
Protein Y is secreted through the classical ER-Golgi route, since brefeldin A mainly blocks endocytosis and leaves exocytosis intact.
Protein Y likely uses an unconventional route that bypasses the Golgi, if a classical cargo control confirms the drug worked.
Protein Y carries a signal peptide, since brefeldin A mainly blocks proteins lacking one and so would not affect it.

rubric: Continued secretion despite Golgi collapse suggests an unconventional route, provided a control cargo shows the drug was effective.
Distractors misstate what brefeldin A does or assume lysis.

items.prompt: A drug makes cells accumulate with 4N DNA content. You must decide which added assay best distinguishes G2 arrest from mitotic arrest.

options.label: Repeat the DNA-content flow analysis at higher resolution, since mitotic cells carry more DNA than G2 cells.
Add phospho-histone H3 (Ser10) staining to the DNA-content analysis, since it marks condensed mitotic chromatin.
Blot for cyclin D1 levels, since cyclin D1 peaks in G2 and then falls as cells enter mitosis.
Measure a short BrdU pulse, since G2 cells are synthesizing DNA and mitotic cells are not.

rubric: G2 and M cells both have 4N DNA; phospho-histone H3 marks mitotic cells specifically.
Distractors misassign DNA amount, S-phase labeling or cyclin D timing.

items.prompt: A GFP-tagged protein overexpressed from a strong promoter shows a mitochondrial signal. How should the claim that it is a native mitochondrial protein be evaluated?

options.label: Inconclusive, since overexpression can mislocalize proteins; fractionate the untagged endogenous protein and probe with an antibody.
Conclusive, since GFP fusions always report native localization when the signal is bright, organelle-shaped and reproducible across cells.
Inconclusive, since GFP is itself a mitochondrial targeting sequence that directs any fusion partner into the organelle when overexpressed.
Conclusive, since overexpression of a non-mitochondrial protein would send it to the nucleus rather than to mitochondria in cells.

rubric: Overexpression and tags can cause artefactual localization, so endogenous protein must be checked.
Distractors assume tags and overexpression are always faithful or that GFP targets mitochondria.

items.prompt: In respirometry, oligomycin cuts oxygen consumption by about 70%. A student says the remaining oligomycin-insensitive consumption is ATP production by an alternative pathway. Which critique is best?

options.label: It reflects maximal respiratory capacity, because oligomycin forces electron flow through the chain by dissipating the proton gradient.
It mainly reflects proton leak and non-mitochondrial oxygen use, because oligomycin blocks ATP synthase and removes ATP-linked respiration.
It reflects substrate-level phosphorylation, because oligomycin blocks only oxidative phosphorylation and leaves glycolytic ATP untouched.
It reflects uncoupled complex I activity, because oligomycin blocks the electron transport chain at complex III and spares complex I.

rubric: Residual respiration after ATP synthase inhibition is leak plus non-mitochondrial consumption, not ATP synthesis.
Distractors misplace oligomycin's target or confuse it with an uncoupler.

items.prompt: A 35 kDa protein fused to GFP (60 kDa total) accumulates in the nucleus, and the authors conclude it is an importin cargo with an NLS. Which are valid criticisms of this conclusion? Select all that apply.

options.label: Fusions of this size can still enter through nuclear pores by passive diffusion, so nuclear signal alone does not show receptor-mediated import.
A dominant-negative Ran mutant or importin inhibitor would discriminate active import from diffusion better than localization alone.
The nuclear envelope has no size selectivity, so any protein equilibrates freely and accumulation is always meaningless.
Only proteins with an NLS can cross the nuclear pore, so nuclear signal proves an NLS is present.
Nuclear accumulation may reflect retention by chromatin binding after entry, rather than active import.

rubric: Passive entry, retention, and lack of a transport-specific perturbation all weaken the conclusion.
Distractors overstate or deny pore selectivity.

items.prompt: Cells treated with tunicamycin for 6 h show raised BiP and spliced XBP1 mRNA, but no increase in cell death. A colleague concludes the unfolded protein response has failed. Which evaluation is best?

options.label: The response has failed, because BiP induction shows chaperone capacity was overwhelmed and cell death is likely already underway.
The response is in its adaptive phase; fate depends on resolution, since sustained stress shifts signaling toward CHOP-driven apoptosis.
The response has already succeeded, because BiP induction restores folding capacity and IRE1 signaling is expected to switch off within hours.
The response is uninformative here, because XBP1 splicing reflects general transcription changes and does not report ER lumen stress.

rubric: Early UPR output is adaptive; apoptosis follows only when stress is unresolved.
Distractors read induction as failure, irrelevance or completion.

items.prompt: You must quantify what fraction of a receptor sits at the plasma membrane in cultured cells, with no signal from internal pools. Which design meets this constraint?

options.label: Label intact cells on ice with membrane-impermeant sulfo-NHS-biotin, lyse, capture on streptavidin beads, and blot against total lysate.
Fractionate cells by differential centrifugation and blot the nuclear pellet for the receptor against a loading control.
Fix and permeabilize cells with methanol, stain with a receptor antibody, and measure total fluorescence per cell.
Lyse cells in Triton X-100, biotinylate all lysate proteins, capture on streptavidin beads, and blot the pulldown for the receptor.

rubric: An impermeant label on intact cells tags only surface proteins.
Distractors label or detect internal pools as well.

items.prompt: Design a reversible arrest of a culture at the G1/S boundary so cells enter S phase together on release, without damaging the spindle. Which plan meets this?

options.label: Starve of serum for 72 h, which holds every cell exactly at G1/S and releases them in S phase together on refeeding.
Hold cells at full confluence, which stalls them at G1/S and releases them synchronously after one replating.
Treat with nocodazole for 16 h, which stalls cells at G1/S by depolymerizing microtubules and reverses on washout.
Apply a double thymidine block with a release between, which depletes dCTP pools and stalls cells at G1/S until washout.

rubric: Double thymidine block arrests at G1/S reversibly through nucleotide pool imbalance.
Nocodazole arrests in M, and starvation or confluence give a broad G0/G1 arrest.

items.prompt: Build a fusion so GFP is imported into the mitochondrial matrix and the targeting sequence is removed afterward. Which design meets both constraints?

options.label: Add an internal classical NLS inside GFP so importin delivers it to the organelle, where proteases cleave the NLS.
Add an N-terminal ER signal peptide upstream of GFP so cotranslational translocation delivers it, where signal peptidase cleaves it.
Add a cleavable N-terminal amphipathic presequence upstream of GFP so TOM/TIM23 deliver it to the matrix, where MPP cleaves it.
Add a C-terminal KDEL sequence after GFP so the fusion is retrieved to the organelle, where it is cleaved on arrival.

rubric: Matrix import uses a cleavable N-terminal presequence with TOM/TIM23 and MPP.
Distractors use ER, retrieval or nuclear signals.

items.prompt: Design a reconstitution to show a purified transporter couples substrate uptake to inward proton flow (H+ symport). Which design is best?

options.label: Dissolve the protein in detergent micelles at neutral pH and measure substrate uptake across the micelle wall over time.
Reconstitute into liposomes, load ATP inside and Mg2+ outside, and measure labeled substrate accumulation against a protein-free control vesicle.
Reconstitute into liposomes, impose an inward H+ gradient, and measure labeled uptake against gradient-free and protein-free controls.
Reconstitute into liposomes with equal pH on both sides, then measure substrate binding by absorbance and compare it to protein-free vesicles.

rubric: A proton gradient plus controls tests coupling in a closed vesicle system.
Distractors lack a gradient, a closed compartment or proper controls.

items.prompt: A proposal shows a kinase inhibitor lowers a phospho-specific antibody signal on substrate S, and concludes the kinase directly phosphorylates S. What is the most important missing element?

options.label: An actin loading control on the blots, since equal loading across lanes would establish that the kinase phosphorylates S directly rather than indirectly.
A higher inhibitor dose and a time course, since a stronger and faster drop in signal would show that the phosphorylation of S is direct.
A non-phosphorylatable S mutant plus an in vitro assay with purified kinase and S, showing the signal is on S and direct.
An antibody to the kinase's autophosphorylation site, since a matching drop in that signal would prove S is a direct substrate of the kinase.

rubric: A site mutant checks antibody specificity and in vitro reconstitution tests directness.
Distractors add dose or loading controls that cannot show directness.

items.prompt: Design an experiment to determine whether the C-terminus of a plasma membrane protein faces the cytosol or the extracellular space. Which elements belong in a valid design? Select all that apply.

options.label: Permeabilize every sample with Triton X-100 before staining, so accessibility is identical in all conditions.
Include a reference membrane protein of known topology to confirm that permeabilization behaves as expected.
Compare antibody staining of nonpermeabilized cells with cells permeabilized gently so the plasma membrane is opened.
Add a C-terminal epitope tag recognized by a specific antibody.
Run denaturing SDS-PAGE of lysate alone, since band size reveals which side the C-terminus faces.

rubric: A tag, a permeabilized versus intact comparison, and a known-topology control together define a valid test.
Permeabilizing everything removes the contrast, and band size does not give orientation.

items.prompt: A lab must track cell-cycle phase in individual living cells for 24 h by time-lapse microscopy, without fixation or DNA dyes, and must see G1 to S transitions. Which design meets all constraints?

options.label: Fix parallel dishes hourly, label with EdU, and infer each living cell's phase from the population averages.
Collect cells hourly for propidium iodide flow cytometry and link each profile to a tracked living cell.
Express FUCCI reporters, Cdt1 and geminin fragments that are degraded in opposite phases, and image live.
Stain with Hoechst every 15 min and read DNA content from intensity to assign phase in each living cell.

rubric: FUCCI reports phase in single live cells through cell-cycle-regulated degradation, with no dyes or fixation.
Distractors use DNA dyes, fixation or destructive sampling.
